title: Yarn-over eyelet triangle shawl
subtitle: A top-down fingering triangle with an eyelet mesh body and garter border.
excerpt: A top-down triangular shawl in fingering-weight wool with an allover 4-row eyelet mesh pattern throughout the body and a 5-row garter border at cast-off. Wingspan 175 cm, centre-back depth 82 cm when blocked. About 380 g of fingering yarn. The eyelet mesh is a simple yo/k2tog repeat that beginner lace knitters can manage.
sourceNotes: Allover yarn-over eyelet mesh is one of the most fundamental lace knitting structures. It appears in Weldon's Practical Knitter, 1st series (1886), §Lace Knitting, and in Mary Thomas's Book of Knitting Patterns (1943), §Open Stitches. The top-down triangle shawl construction follows Elizabeth Zimmermann, Knitting Without Tears (1971).

glossaryTerms.definition: An allover lace structure made up of yarn-over increases paired with k2tog decreases, arranged in a regular grid. The result is an even, open fabric with round holes at every yarn-over position.
A small strip of garter stitch worked on a few stitches, rotated and picked up to form the centre-back starting point of a top-down triangle shawl.

content.text: A top-down triangular shawl in fingering-weight wool with an allover
eyelet mesh
body and a 5-row garter border at the cast-off edge. Wingspan 175 cm, depth 82 cm.

The eyelet mesh pattern is worked across the full body on RS rows: the repeat is *yo, k2tog; repeat from * across. On WS rows, all stitches are knitted (garter mesh). The 4-row yo increase rows follow the standard top-down triangle schedule. A
garter tab
starts the shawl at the centre back neck. Budget about 380 g (about 1,520 m / 1,660 yards) of fingering wool.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: About 380 g (1,520 m / 1,660 yards) of fingering-weight yarn

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3.75 mm (UK 9 / US 5) circular needle, 100 cm or longer

items.name: Tapestry needle, scissors, blocking mat, pins

content.text: Gauge

24 stitches and 48 rows to 10 cm over stockinette on 3.75 mm needles, blocked. The eyelet mesh gauge matches stockinette gauge closely because every yarn-over pairs with a k2tog to maintain stitch count. If your blocked gauge reads 26 stitches per 10 cm, the wingspan at the same row count will be about 161 cm. Work 18 extra RS increase rows to compensate.
Stitches used
Pattern
Garter tab
Work the garter tab: 3 sts on waste yarn, 6 rows garter, switch to main yarn, pick up 9 sts total. Place markers: after st 1, after st 5 (centre), before st 9.
Body
RS row: k1, yo, SM, yo, k2tog across to 1 st before centre marker, SM, yo, k1 (centre st), yo, SM, yo, k2tog across to last st, SM, yo, k1. (4 sts added per RS row)
WS row: k all sts.
The eyelet mesh (yo, k2tog) runs across the full wing sections on every RS row. Continue until wingspan reaches 175 cm (approximately 210 RS rows at gauge, giving 9 + (4 × 210) = 849 stitches).
Garter border
After the final RS body row, work 5 WS garter rows (knit every row, no increases). This sets the garter border.
Bind off
Work Jeny's surprisingly stretchy bind-off on a RS row. Binding off on a plain RS row (not a mesh row) gives a neater top edge.
Stitch count check-ins
After 50 RS rows: 9 + 200 = 209 stitches. Each wing holds 103 stitches. The eyelet mesh should be clearly visible and regular.
After 150 RS rows: 9 + 600 = 609 stitches. Wingspan approximately 130 cm. The shawl is about three-quarters done.
Common faults

Mesh misaligned from row to row: the yo/k2tog pairs were not offset by 1 stitch between RS rows, so the holes don't sit diagonally. On the first RS mesh row start the repeat at st 1; on the second, start at st 2. Alternating the offset creates the diagonal mesh grid.

Holes at the increase yo positions lost in the mesh: the 4 increase yarn-overs at the markers must be treated as plain increases (not paired with a k2tog). Keep 2 stitches clear on each side of every marker for the increase structure.
Blocking

Soak in cool water 15 minutes, press out in towels. Pin the wings to the full 175 cm wingspan and pin the straight cast-off edge. The eyelet mesh opens visibly: the blocked shawl will look 20% more open than the wet-pressed unblocked fabric.
Care
Hand wash in cool water, lay flat to dry. Re-block after a few wears to restore the mesh openness.
What to try next
Swap the eyelet mesh for a bird's-eye mesh (yo, ssk). This gives opposite-direction meshes on the two wings, flowing away from the spine.
